summary: Root cause identified with high confidence (0.82): the shared redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 failed its PING health check at 13:22:10Z and the replica promoted in its place was mid-resync and therefore empty, producing a cache-miss storm that forced market-data-service to synchronously rebuild quotes from the exchange-feed snapshot (up to 8748ms), saturating its CPU and pushing its p99 past pricing-engine's computation deadline, which surfaced as 2-3s quote loads on trading screens. The origin hop is verified by cache-layer telemetry: hit_ratio_pct collapsed 95.9% -> 10.82% at 13:22Z while memory_pct fell 71% -> 6.1% and connected_clients fell ~295 -> 40 (an empty/new-primary signature), with evictions flat, plus an explicit failover log naming redis-cache-3 as promoted with an empty dataset. Competing origins were actively falsified: request rates at market-data-service and pricing-engine were flat across onset (no load spike), exchange-gateway and its upstream feed were flat, and no deployment or config change exists anywhere in the blast radius. Why redis-cache-2 failed its health check is not determined and remains a residual uncertainty, but it sits above the identified origin and does not change the mitigation.

ranked_hypotheses.title: redis-cache primary failed and an empty replica was promoted, causing a cache-miss storm that forces market-data-service rebuilds and propagates as pricing-engine quote latency
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The fault originates at the shared redis-cache layer: the primary node redis-cache-2 failed its health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts) and was marked down at 13:22:10Z; the replica promoted in its place was mid-resync and therefore EMPTY (explicit WARN 'dataset on new primary is empty'). The promoted node's dataset loss is confirmed by telemetry: memory_pct dropped 71% -> 6.1% and connected_clients fell ~295 -> 40 simultaneously, with hit_ratio_pct collapsing ~95% -> 10.82% at exactly 13:22Z. market-data-service therefore misses quote:<n> keys and synchronously rebuilds each quote from the exchange-feed snapshot (up to 8748ms), saturating its CPU (~90%) and blowing its p99, which makes pricing-engine's market-data call exceed its computation deadline ('quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms'), producing 2-3s quote loads on trading screens. This is the HIST-107 mechanism ('Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica') reproduced exactly, but with no recorded deployment or config change triggering it — it is an unrecorded infrastructure event.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 fails health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts) and is marked down at 13:22:10Z; the promoted replica redis-cache-3 is mid-resync and EMPTY ('dataset on new primary is empty')

The empty promoted dataset is confirmed at the metric layer: hit_ratio_pct collapses from ~94.7-97% (through the 13:20Z bucket) to 10.82% at 13:22Z, memory_pct drops 71% -> 6.1%, connected_clients collapses ~295 -> 40 — an empty/new-primary signature, not load or eviction
The cache-loss is NOT eviction-driven: evictions_per_min stays flat ~2.0-4.9 keys/min across 12:50-14:29Z with no burst at onset, so the hit-ratio collapse is key loss, not memory pressure
market-data-service now misses quote:<n> keys and logs 'cache miss storm ... rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot', 289 WARNs from 13:22:25Z, rebuilds up to 8748ms
The synchronous rebuild path saturates market-data-service CPU (~45% -> ~90% sustained) and its p99 jumps to ~1161ms avg / 1980ms max from ~40ms baseline in the same 13:20Z onset bucket
pricing-engine's slow call is market-data-service: 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' (192 errors, first_seen 13:23:57Z)
pricing-engine p99 jumps from ~58-62ms to 1370-2218ms with error_rate rising to ~4% in the 13:15-13:20Z onset window
blended client effects: client reconnect storm (15048 new connections in 10s, 13:30:20Z) and contractile tables hold the elevated latency
Sales/app trading screens report 2-3s quote loads

assumptions: The trigger for the redis-cache-2 PING health-check failure (host, network, or resource) is not determined — redis-cache logs begin at the 13:22:10Z health-check failure.

redis-cache exposes no latency_p99_ms metric (F24), so cache-side latency is not directly measurable; the failover -> miss -> rebuild chain is inferred from logs + hit-ratio/memory/client telemetry rather than measured cache latency.

The p99 step is observed in the 13:20Z metric bucket and the failover log at 13:22:10Z — bucket granularity means the app-layer bucket may aggregate some pre-failover sub-intervals; the cache-miss WARN burst (13:22:25Z) and hit-ratio collapse (13:22Z) bracket the failover tightly and are causally downstream of it.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Load-driven saturation at market-data-service (rebuild path) exceeds provisioned capacity — no change needed
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The origin is capacity/resource saturation in market-data-service: synchronous snapshot rebuilds from the exchange feed are CPU-expensive and at market-open-scale load the rebuild path saturates market-data-service CPU (~90% sustained), so its p99 rises and pricing-engine's deadline is exceeded. Redis misses appear because market-data-service is hammering a cold/under-sized cache under this load, not because redis failed.

causal_chain.claim: Load on the quote/rebuild path exceeds market-data-service provisioned capacity at market open
market-data-service inbound request_rate rises at onset, driving the rebuild path
market-data-service CPU saturates (~90% sustained from 13:20Z) and p99 rises to ~1161ms avg
Cache-miss warnings + slow snapshot rebuilds indicate the expensive rebuild path is being exercised heavily
pricing-engine's market-data-service call exceeds deadline; p99 ~2s, error_rate ~4%

assumptions: A traffic spike occurred at onset.
Cache misses are a symptom of high traffic rather than a cause.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly contradicted by load telemetry: market-data-service inbound request_rate is flat across onset (13:16Z avg 946.42, 13:18Z trough 932.99, 13:20Z 992.73 — within the day's normal 909-1025 band) (F25, F26), and pricing-engine request_rate is likewise flat (F27). Load did not rise. The cache-layer evidence points the other way from this hypothesis: the hit-ratio collapse is accompanied by a simultaneous memory/client footprint collapse and an EXPLICIT, logged failover to an empty replica (F19, F21, F22), and evictions did NOT spike (F20) — i.e. the misses are key loss, not a hammered under-sized cache. Redis CPU stayed flat (F12) and exchange-side remained healthy (F28-F30), so no load-failure origin is supported.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unenumerated change on an unqueried trading-path service (order-service / exchange-gateway / api-gateway) or on pricing-engine itself
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The fault originates in a component of the trading path whose change history was never enumerated: order-service, exchange-gateway or api-gateway, or pricing-engine itself, deployed or reconfigured near 13:15-13:20Z. Per-channel change coverage was incomplete, so a change there could be hiding.

That component adds latency on the market-data call path (exchange-gateway backs market-data-service)
market-data-service p99 + CPU spike and a cache-miss storm appear
pricing-engine deadline-exceeded and screen latency

assumptions: A change exists but was not captured by the queried change inventory.
Such a change could produce an empty-replica redis failover and cache-miss storm, which no code/config change mechanism would naturally cause.

Moreover the observed mechanism (empty replica promoted after a PING health-check failure, memory/client footprint collapse) is an infrastructure event with no plausible code/config-change pathway (F22, F21), and exchange-gateway — the adjacent service this hypothesis most depends on — shows flat latency/error and flat upstream feed health across onset (F28, F29, F30).

ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only deployment in the 48h window — auth-service v7.2.0 'Session cookie hardening' (SameSite=strict) at 11:30Z — caused the quote-latency degradation via session re-validation or a shared edge/gateway effect.

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Decisively contradicted: (a) SCOPE — auth-service is absent from pricing-engine's and market-data-service's dependency graphs, and every component in the observed blast radius has zero recorded changes (F3, F16, F15); (b) TIMING — precedes onset by ~1h45-1h50m with a flat 58-62ms p99 through 13:15Z (F7, F13); (c) MECHANISM — errors name market-data-service as the slow callee and a redis cache-miss storm, nothing login/session-related (F8, F11), and the cache-layer evidence now shows an explicit redis failover (F22) with no connection to auth.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Genuine resource exhaustion (memory) on pricing-engine itself
ranked_hypotheses.statement: pricing-engine's own memory/resource pressure caused the deadline-exceeded errors and slow quotes, independent of market-data-service.

causal_chain.claim: pricing-engine memory/CPU pressure
pricing-engine p99 >2s

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted by mechanism and metrics: pricing-engine CPU stayed flat ~38-41% with no saturation trend (F12); the error signature explicitly names market-data-service as the slow callee (F8); the same-onset p99/CPU jump and cache-miss storm appear in market-data-service (F10, F11); and an explicit redis failover is logged (F22). A pricing-engine-internal resource cause cannot explain the concurrent redis failover, cache-miss storm, and market-data-service CPU saturation.

recommended_actions.action: Verify the redis-cache failover and its blast radius now: confirm redis-cache-3 is primary and fully resynced, confirm hit_ratio_pct has recovered to ~95%+ and memory_pct/connected_clients are back to baseline, and confirm market-data-service CPU has returned to ~45% and its cache-miss WARN burst has stopped. If hit ratio is still low, force a controlled full resync/warm-up of the promoted primary before declaring mitigation.
recommended_actions.rationale: The identified mechanism is an empty promoted replica (F22) causing misses (F19, F20, F21) and rebuild saturation (F10, F11); mitigation is complete only when the dataset is restored and misses stop. Recovery activity was already partly visible (full resync 13:28:42Z, client reconnect storm 13:30:20Z, F22).

recommended_actions.action: Add stampede/single-flight protection on the market-data-service redis-miss rebuild path (e.g. per-quote-key lock or request coalescing, plus bounded concurrency on exchange-feed snapshot rebuilds) so a cold cache cannot drive synchronous rebuilds to saturate market-data-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: The verified failure mode is synchronous per-quote rebuilds (up to 8748ms) driving market-data-service CPU to ~90% and blowing pricing-engine's deadline (F11, F10, F8). Coalescing would decouple cache-miss volume from downstream CPU even while the cache is cold.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument and alarm on redis-cache dataset/failover health: alert on any failover promotion with an empty or non-resynced dataset (the 'dataset on new primary is empty' WARN), and on hit_ratio_pct dropping below a threshold (e.g. <80% for >1 min). Note that redis-cache currently exposes no latency metric, so hit_ratio/memory/clients are the available leading indicators.
recommended_actions.rationale: The degradation was detected via downstream p99 and deadline-exceeded errors rather than cache-layer health; the explicit empty-dataset WARN at 13:22:52Z (F22) and hit-ratio collapse to 10.82% (F19) were the earliest unambiguous signals but had no alert. redis-cache has no latency_p99_ms metric (F24).

recommended_actions.action: Harden redis-cache failover semantics: refuse to promote a replica that is mid-resync / has an empty dataset, or require the promoted node to complete resync (or be repopulated from a warm source) before accepting client traffic; review persistence (AOF/RDB) configuration on redis-cache-2/3.
recommended_actions.rationale: The proximate fault is promotion of a replica whose dataset was empty because it was resyncing (F22); preventing empty promotion removes the root mechanism entirely rather than mitigating its symptoms.

recommended_actions.action: Determine why redis-cache-2 failed 3 consecutive PING health checks and capture the failing host's node-level metrics/logs (host, network, resource); this is the unexplained trigger above the identified origin.
recommended_actions.rationale: Logs begin at the 13:22:10Z health-check failure (F22); the trigger of the primary failure is not determined and is the remaining uncertainty on this root cause.

recommended_actions.action: Close the change-inventory blind spot by enumerating deployments/config changes for order-service, exchange-gateway, api-gateway and pricing-engine individually, and confirm the aggregate 'count 1' result remains stable.
recommended_actions.rationale: The rejection of the change-based hypotheses rests on an aggregate all-services query plus two per-service queries, with a first attempt returning partial:true (F2, F4); direct per-service confirmation is needed to close this gap.

recommended_actions.action: Add a downstream-caller observability check (trading screen/app tier and gateway) to quantify the user-visible impact and confirm only the quote path was affected.
recommended_actions.rationale: The symptom was reported 'across trading screens' but no downstream caller metrics/logs were retrieved; blast radius beyond pricing-engine and market-data-service is unverified.

recommended_actions.action: Rehearse/test the redis failover path with a mid-resync replica in a game-day, and ensure warm-up/repopulation of quote keys (or a secondary cache tier) is part of the runbook so a failover cannot present an empty dataset to market-data-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is a reproduction of HIST-107 ('Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica') on the same shared redis-cache dependency (F17, F5), so without a structural fix the same class of incident is expected to recur.

data_gaps: The trigger of the redis-cache-2 PING health-check failure is unknown: redis-cache logs begin at the 13:22:10Z failure, so host/network/resource cause of the primary failure could not be determined (limits conclusions about preventing the next occurrence, not about the mechanism).

redis-cache exposes no latency_p99_ms metric (only connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct), so cache-side latency during the failover could not be quantified; the miss -> rebuild chain is established from logs and hit-ratio/memory/client telemetry rather than measured cache latency.

Deployments/config changes were not enumerated per-service for order-service, exchange-gateway, api-gateway or pricing-engine individually (only an aggregate all-services query, which returned partial:true on first attempt but partial:false with count 1 on retry, plus two per-service queries). A change on an unqueried trading-path service therefore cannot be fully ruled out.

No logs or metrics were pulled for downstream callers of pricing-engine (trading screens / app tier / gateway), so the full blast radius of the slow quotes is unverified.

what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that market-data-service's cache-miss storm was caused by key loss from eviction or expiry rather than an empty promoted dataset: e.g. a redis-cache eviction/expiry burst at 13:20-13:22Z (currently falsified — evictions stayed flat ~2-5/min, F20), or an explicit expire/TTL purge log rather than the 'dataset on new primary is empty' failover log (F22).

Direct measurement showing redis-cache remained serving the quote keys during 13:20-13:30Z (e.g. hit_ratio_pct staying ~95% at 13:22Z), which would implicate a market-data-service-internal or pricing-engine-internal cause instead.

findings.statement: redis-cache CPU stayed flat at ~21-22% across 13:00-14:55Z (min 20.34, max 24.37), so the cache host itself shows no saturation trend; pricing-engine CPU likewise stayed ~38-41% (39.7 mean), i.e. neither the cache nor pricing-engine compute looks saturated.

The only deployment in the 24-48h window across ALL services is auth-service v7.2.0 (dep-5604), deployed_at 2026-04-09T11:30:00Z, summary 'Session cookie hardening', change 'SameSite=strict', status live, rolled_back_at null. Its timestamp PRECEDES the p99 onset of 13:15-13:20Z by ~1h45-1h50m; it was never rolled back.
Zero config/feature-flag changes across all services in 2026-04-09T09:00Z-15:00Z (count 0), so no flag flip can be correlated with the 13:15-13:20Z onset.

No deployments exist for pricing-engine (count 0, 2026-04-08T00:00Z-15:00Z), matching the report's claim 'No releases to pricing today'; no deployments for market-data-service (count 0) or config changes for redis-cache (count 0) in the incident window.

SCOPE MISMATCH: dep-5604 touches auth-service, which is absent from pricing-engine's dependency graph (outgoing http market-data-service, cache redis-cache; incoming order-service), and market-data-service's dependencies are redis-cache + exchange-gateway. Nothing in the observed blast radius (pricing-engine, market-data-service, redis-cache) changed.

Historical precedent matching the symptom EXACTLY: HIST-107 (2025-12-09) 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' on redis-cache + market-data-service, symptoms 'cache miss storm','quote latency', root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica' (match_score 7) — same shared dependency and same cache-miss-storm signature seen at 13:22:25Z. HIST-101 shows auth-service releases CAN cause latency (bad_deployment, rolled back), but that incident's symptoms were login-side. These are leads only, not evidence about INC-006.

findings.statement: Ranked shortlist: (1) NO change is temporally tight AND scope-matched — the change record is empty for every component in the blast radius, so no correlating change exists in the data. (2) auth-service dep-5604 is the closest in time (11:30Z) but is a coincidental/low-plausibility candidate: it precedes onset by ~1h45m, auth-service is not a dependency of pricing-engine or market-data-service, and HIST-101-type auth breakage manifests as login failures, not quote latency. (3) The redis-cache cold-cache mechanism (HIST-107 pattern) is a dependency-side risk with NO corresponding recorded change, so it would be an unrecorded infrastructure event, not a deployment.

redis-cache hit_ratio_pct was stable at ~94.7-97% through the 13:20:00Z bucket, then COLLAPSED to 10.82% at 13:22:00Z and stayed low (12.28% at 13:24Z, 14.26% at 13:29Z). The 13:00/13:15/13:17/13:20 buckets were all normal (~95-96%).

redis-cache evictions_per_min did NOT spike at onset: it stayed flat/steady ~2.0-4.9 keys/min across 12:50-14:29Z (13:17Z 3.25, 13:20Z 2.98, 13:23Z 3.49, 13:26Z 2.26), i.e. NO eviction burst. The hit-ratio collapse was not caused by eviction pressure.

redis-cache memory_pct dropped abruptly from ~71% at 13:20Z to 6.1% at 13:22Z and connected_clients fell from ~295 (13:17Z) to 40.24 at 13:23Z and then recovered to ~310 by 13:26Z. A simultaneous collapse of memory footprint and clients is consistent with an EMPTY dataset/new primary, not a load or eviction event.

findings.statement: The redis-cache hit-ratio collapse (13:22:00Z bucket) sits in the SAME onset window as pricing-engine p99 jump (13:20Z bucket, F7) and market-data-service 'cache miss storm' WARN burst (first_seen 13:22:25Z, F11) — the cache-layer event is tightly coincident with (within ~2 min of) the application-layer symptoms.

redis-cache exposes exactly these metrics: connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct. There is NO 'latency_p99_ms' metric for redis-cache — cache latency is not directly observable; cpu_pct (F12: flat ~21-22%) is the closest host-health signal.
